chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatam narrated to us, saying: Al-Fadl ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Al-Haytham ibn Kumayl narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr narrated, from Ziyad ibn Khaythamah, from Sa'd ibn Qays al-Hamdani, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"The affairs of this nation will remain upright, and they will be victorious over their enemies, until twelve Caliphs pass away, all of them from Quraysh." I went to him in his house and asked, "Then what will happen?" He said, "Then there will be chaos (al-harj)."
ai.seo_question: What happens after the twelve Caliphs from Quraysh according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal establishes the foundational Shia doctrine of the Twelve Imams, identifying them as the legitimate successors who maintain the community's spiritual and political integrity. The transition to 'al-harj' (chaos) following their era underscores the eschatological significance of the Mahdi's reappearance as the restorer of justice after the period of occultation and strife.
